page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-288-metal is a bare-metal server instance featuring 288 vCPUs mapped to 144 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor. Operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz, this x86_64 architecture CPU includes a 504 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). The system is equipped with 1080 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 6 GHz, providing 3.75 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark evaluations place this server in the top tier for multi-core CPU performance, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and passmark CPU physics. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, with cached read-only small block speeds reaching 23,040.71 GB/sec and uncached large block read speeds at 1,087.82 GB/sec, both ranking in the top tier. Database operations and Redis SET operations also perform in the top tier, executing 413.48 million operations per second. However, single-core CPU performance and image processing fall into the average tier, and text generation for small language models is in the bottom tier.

From a resource density perspective, the c4-standard-288-metal offers high compute density and memory bandwidth relative to its hardware class, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for highly parallelized workloads that do not require local storage or GPU acceleration. The lack of local NVMe storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which is a key architectural tradeoff. This server is highly suitable for large-scale database operations, heavy CPU-based simulations, software compilation, and multi-threaded data processing workloads.
